name: sso-oidc
description: IAM Identity Center OpenID Connect (OIDC) is a web service that enables a client (such as CLI or a native application) to register with IAM Identity Center.

subcommands.name: create-token
subcommands.description: Creates and returns access and refresh tokens for clients that are authenticated using client secrets.

options.name: --client-id
options.description: The unique identifier string for the client or application. This value comes from the result of the RegisterClient API

options.name: --client-secret
options.description: A secret string generated for the client. This value should come from the persisted result of the RegisterClient API

options.name: --grant-type
options.description: Supports the following OAuth grant types: Device Code and Refresh Token.

options.name: --device-code
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Device Code grant type. This short-term code is used to identify this authorization request.

options.name: --code
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type. The short-term code is used to identify this authorization request.

options.name: --refresh-token
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Refresh Token grant type. This token is used to refresh short-term tokens, such as the access token, that might expire.

options.name: --scope
options.description: The list of scopes for which authorization is requested. The access token that is issued is limited to the scopes that are granted.

options.name: --redirect-uri
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type.

options.name: --code-verifier
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: create-token-with-iam
subcommands.description: Creates and returns access and refresh tokens for clients and applications that are authenticated using IAM entities.

options.name: --client-id
options.description: The unique identifier string for the client or application. This value is an application ARN that has OAuth grants configured

options.name: --grant-type
options.description: Supports the following OAuth grant types: Authorization Code, Refresh Token, JWT Bearer, and Token Exchange.

options.name: --code
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type. This short-term code is used to identify this authorization request.

options.name: --refresh-token
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Refresh Token grant type. This token is used to refresh short-term tokens, such as the access token, that might expire.

options.name: --assertion
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the JWT Bearer grant type. This value specifies the JSON Web Token (JWT) issued by a trusted token issuer.

options.name: --scope
options.description: The list of scopes for which authorization is requested. The access token that is issued is limited to the scopes that are granted.

options.name: --redirect-uri
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type.

options.name: --subject-token
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Token Exchange grant type. This value specifies the subject of the exchange.

options.name: --subject-token-type
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Token Exchange grant type. This value specifies the type of token that is passed as the subject of the exchange.

options.name: --requested-token-type
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Token Exchange grant type. This value specifies the type of token that the requester can receive.

options.name: --code-verifier
options.description: Used only when calling this API for the Authorization Code grant type.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: register-client
subcommands.description: Registers a client with IAM Identity Center. This allows clients to initiate device authorization.

options.name: --client-name
options.description: The friendly name of the client

options.name: --client-type
options.description: The type of client. The service supports only public as a client type. Anything other than public will be rejected by the service

options.name: --scopes
options.description: The list of scopes that are defined by the client. Upon authorization, this list is used to restrict permissions when granting an access token

options.name: --redirect-uris
options.description: The list of redirect URI that are defined by the client.

options.name: --grant-types
options.description: The list of OAuth 2.0 grant types that are defined by the client. This list is used to restrict the token granting flows available to the client

options.name: --issuer-url
options.description: The IAM Identity Center Issuer URL associated with an instance of IAM Identity Center. This value is needed for user access to resources through the client

options.name: --entitled-application-arn
options.description: This IAM Identity Center application ARN is used to define administrator-managed configuration for public client access to resources.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: start-device-authorization
subcommands.description: Initiates device authorization by requesting a pair of verification codes from the authorization service

options.name: --client-id
options.description: The unique identifier string for the client that is registered with IAM Identity Center.

options.name: --client-secret
options.description: A secret string that is generated for the client. This value should come from the persisted result of the RegisterClient API operation

options.name: --start-url
options.description: The URL for the Amazon Web Services access portal. For more information, see Using the Amazon Web Services access portal in the IAM Identity Center User Guide
